notes.key_messages: Candidates should read the questions carefully, as they often contain specific information that must be used in the answer. For example, when the question asks for two lines to join boxes, only two lines should be drawn. It is important that candidates write clearly and spell scientific terms correctly. Candidates also need to be careful about how they write their numbers. Command words such as ‘describe’, ‘explain’, ‘suggest’ and ‘compare’ require different responses from candidates. If a description of a graph or table is required, then data should be used in the description given. Many candidates can do this effectively, although some do not include units or they give general answers rather than precise ones. An explanation requires more than just a description and candidates should be encouraged to practise the difference between ‘explain’ and ‘describe’. Correct spelling of certain words is expected e.g., uterus, ureter, and urethra.
notes.general_comments: Many candidates were well prepared for the exam and had obviously referred to past papers and mark schemes when preparing. This type of preparation enables candidates to express themselves more clearly.
notes.1ai: Many candidates were not accurate enough when labelling the different features, particularly the cell wall. Label lines should not have arrow heads. The plasmid was often identified incorrectly.
notes.1aii: Many candidates did not read the question correctly and gave features of a bacterial cell e.g., cell wall rather than characteristics of living organisms shown by bacteria.
notes.1bi: Most candidates answered correctly but some were confused by the first part, stating infected ‘with gonorrhoea’.
notes.1bii: Many candidates found the calculation demanding.
notes.1c: Lots of candidates used the word immune rather than resistant.
notes.1d: This question was generally well answered although some candidates stated ‘use protection’ rather than giving appropriate examples. Do not have sexual relations with lots of people was a common answer which did gain credit as it is too general.
notes.2ai: Most candidates were able to correctly identify the phloem and xylem, although a few candidates got them the wrong way round.
notes.2aii: Very few correctly identified the cortex cells. Incorrect answers included all parts of a plant.
notes.2b: Very few candidates gave an answer which mentioned structure or support. Most candidates stated transport of water but many also stated transport of sucrose.
notes.2ci: Some candidates put root rather than root hair.
notes.2cii: This question was generally well answered but several stated absorption rather than osmosis.
notes.2ciii: Most candidates knew that the structure increases the surface area.
notes.2d: Most candidates knew that diffusion involved substances moving down a concentration gradient but many also thought that this required energy.
notes.2e: Few candidates were able to name mitochondria as the site of aerobic respiration, instead stating various plant structures.
notes.3ai: Few candidates were able to name the adrenal gland, most offering adrenaline or kidney instead. Many knew that that the testes secrete testosterone.
notes.3aii: Very few candidates were able to describe a hormone. Those that did know it was a chemical and was transported by the blood were often confused about where it acts.
notes.3aiii: Most knew that hormones act more slowly than the nervous system.
notes.3b: Most gained all four marks, although some were confused about the diameter of the pupil increasing to let in more light.
notes.4a: Many candidates were not able to give the word equation for photosynthesis. Some gave the respiration equation. A few candidates tried to write a symbol equation. If this was completely correct, marks were awarded.
notes.4bi: (ii) Many candidates were able to name the pigment but not the structure. Other candidates got them the wrong way round.
notes.4ci: Very few candidates were awarded full marks. It was important to read the question carefully as a whole number was asked for.
notes.4cii: This question was a describe and explain so it is important that both parts of the question are answered in order to gain full marks. It was quite well answered with most candidates able to describe the graph, although some did not recognise that this question was about photosynthesis.
notes.5ai: Most candidates correctly identified the ovary. Fewer could identify the sites of fertilisation and implantation.
notes.5aii: Many candidates could not identify structure N as the cervix. Most correctly identified structure L as the uterus.
notes.5b: Candidates found this a demanding question. Some candidates suggested it was large, had a large surface area or it was stationary. Some gave the features of a sperm.
notes.6a: This question on variation was generally well answered.
notes.6bi: Candidates found this a demanding question. Many just repeated the first stage (that was given in the question). Some candidates clearly did not understand the term drought tolerance, others suggested giving the plants plenty of water. The question needed a description of selective breeding.
notes.6bii: Few candidates correctly stated selective breeding, many saying mutation or adaptation.
notes.6ci: Most answered correctly although some gave both parts of the name or just the species name.
notes.6cii: Many were awarded full marks on this question. A common mistake was to identify the yellow-spotted flower plant as Bb but then go on to complete the Punnet square correctly.
notes.7a: A few candidates were able to identify the correct pyramids, but most found this challenging.
notes.7bi: Some candidates could identify the correct answer.
notes.7bii: ,(iii) The concept of trophic levels was not well understood with very few able to interpret the food web correctly.
notes.7c: Only a few correct responses were seen.
notes.7d: Most could give at least one way in which endangered species could be conserved, although most thought this question was still about the food web earlier in the question.
notes.7e: Many candidates gave answers that were too vague and could not be credited.
